search_queries: targeted: expat, libxml2, mxml, yxml, libroxml, ezxml, sxmlc
ranking_metric: Debian popcon installations of the lead's runtime library binary package (max when two sonames are listed)
selection: expat has the highest Debian popcon count among format-aware C XML parsers (libexpat1 297,134) ahead of libxml2 (libxml2 binary 290,724); Homebrew 365-day installs agree (expat 1,360,500, libxml2 564,778).
uncertainty: Pilot cell: one third-party path (expat 2.10.0) was built, matched the exact namespace-resolved summary of both valid controls under LLVM source coverage, and has native AFL++ feedback with a stable valid-control differential. The expected libxml2 lead ranks second by 6,410 installs (2.2%) on the binary-package metric; it is the obvious next entry, was only smoke-run in a scratch build, and is not verified here. The Debian sourcemax table would invert the order (libxml2 source 61,109) only because the libxml2 source now builds libxml2-16 and the older libxml2 binary is no longer attributed to it, so binary runtime-library counts are the primary metric. Popcon counts installations, mostly pulled in as dependencies (expat by Python, fontconfig and others), not direct parser use. Search was the Conan Center recipe-name substring 'xml' (9 hits, 1 of them a C XML parser) plus seven targeted C names; Conan and Debian miss vendored single-file parsers. The control oracle (controls/xml/check_controls.py) uses Python's pyexpat, the same expat engine, so the match is cross-checked by the Go encoding/xml paths and the scratch libxml2 run. The harness pins XML_SetHashSalt so AFL++ maps are reproducible; this changes only hash-table seeding. ISO C documents no XML API. Two valid UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity, encoding, XML 1.1 or rejection behaviour.
